html:
The Klickitat, who call themselves Qwû'lh-hwai-pûm, are a Sahaptin-speaking people of south-central Washington, living along the Klickitat River north of the Columbia and on the slopes of Mount Adams. They were known as traders and travellers, carrying goods between the Columbia and Puget Sound and west of the Cascades.

They fished salmon at the Columbia falls and gathered roots and berries in the mountains, trading with the Chinook downriver. After epidemics emptied much of the Willamette Valley in the 1830s, some Klickitat moved south into the land of the Kalapuya. In 1855 their leaders signed the treaty that created the Yakama Nation, and most Klickitat are now enrolled there.
